key_insight: Spatially patterned spin rotations accelerate imaginary-time relaxation by redistributing spectral weight away from slow modes while preserving initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes.
engineering_relevance: Twist-based initial-state design offers a controllable strategy for accelerating quantum ground-state preparation.
method: Apply spatially modulated local rotations to select excitation modes.
Use compact-boson theory to derive exact relaxation-crossing times.
Reintroduce slow-mode weight to systematically delay the imaginary-time Mpemba effect.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation in interacting XXZ chains and ladders, plus a 12-qubit variational imaginary-time simulation reproducing relaxation reversals and controlled delays.
watch_item: Scalability and robustness to hardware noise remain unestablished by the reported 12-qubit simulation.
paper_title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
